source.title: Stressor controllability and learned helplessness: The roles of the dorsal raphe nucleus, serotonin, and corticotropin-releasing factor

confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily replicated mechanistic review establishing that the learned-helplessness phenotype is gated by stressor UNCONTROLLABILITY and instantiated by dorsal-raphe 5-HT sensitization + CRF, with vmPFC controllability-detection as the inhibitory gate. Directly anchors the SUFFERING pole of the differentiation: the stop/withdrawal here is an aversive, controllability-contingent escape-failure -- categorically not an effort/energy accumulator. High source_quality; mapping is to the ANTECEDENT and SUBSTRATE contrast rather than to a numeric REE metric, so mapping_fidelity is strong-but-conceptual.
failure_signatures: If a fatigue/stop-recover signal were registered on the SD-011 suffering side, it would inherit controllability-gating and DRN/CRF aversive semantics that the biology assigns ONLY to uncontrollable aversive stress -- mis-attributing an energy-budget stop to a harm/escape-failure mechanism.

Helplessness-driven withdrawal does NOT remit with rest (it requires controllability experience or pharmacological reversal); any model that lets rest dissipate a suffering-side stop signal contradicts this literature.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The behavioral deficits of 'learned helplessness' are produced by the UNCONTROLLABILITY of an aversive stressor (not its mere presence). Uncontrollability is detected by ventromedial prefrontal cortex; when control is absent, the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonergic system is intensely activated and sensitized, and corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) acts in/around the DRN, yielding the escape-failure / passivity phenotype. Controllability engages vmPFC top-down inhibition of the DRN, preventing the deficit.
mapping.ree_translation: This grounds REE's SD-011 (dual nociceptive / aversive) pole, the antecedent of suffering-driven withdrawal: an AVERSIVE, controllability-contingent signal whose 'stop/disengage' output is escape-failure. It defines what fatigue/stop-recover is NOT, supporting the recommendation that a homeostatic fatigue signal register on the SD-012 side, distinct from z_harm_a/SD-011.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rodent shuttlebox/escape paradigms; REE has no DRN/CRF homolog and no explicit serotonergic neuromodulator. The transfer is at the level of ANTECEDENT (uncontrollable aversion) and DYNAMICS (no rest-recovery), not a circuit-level import. REE's z_harm_a is a nociceptive stream, not a controllability-gated 5-HT sensitization process, so even the SD-011 mapping is partial.
mapping.source_context: Review of rodent stressor-controllability paradigms (escapable vs yoked-inescapable shock), DRN single-unit + pharmacology + vmPFC inactivation studies.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality near-ceiling (canonical, replicated). Mapping_fidelity high for the antecedent/dynamics contrast but conceptual, not metric. Transfer_risk moderate: rodent->REE substrate has no serotonergic homolog, but the load-bearing claim (uncontrollable-aversion antecedent, no rest-recovery) transfers as a category boundary, which is what the differentiation needs.
